applicability.action: report an error for a PackageReference/ProjectReference/PackageVersion start tag with unclosed/mismatched quotes or an unquoted value, instead of skipping it
applicability.exceptions: not full XML validation; comments/conditions not evaluated

distinguishing_scenario: A PackageReference with an unquoted Include and no version: no registered rule is violated, the checker reports 'is not well-formed XML ... fix it so the manifest can be checked'.
proposed_clause_text: A PackageReference, ProjectReference or PackageVersion element with malformed attribute quoting is reported as an error (never skipped), so the manifest is not accepted until it can be checked.
rationale: check-dependencies.cjs:102-106 verified (comment: 'an error, so it is never accepted silently'). Both Claude runs described this fail-closed parsing in coverage ledgers but registered no constraint; the K0 groups cover version placement (FG-K0-b104215be5, FG-K0-8aea50ed37), comment/condition handling (FG-K0-15e0f8cf2b) and when checks run (FG-K0-3369be1736). A malformed element fails the check even without any version or dependency violation, so this is a distinct, designed acceptance gate of the enforcement layer.
status_note: Proposal only: not a confirmed EXTRA, not an oracle mapping, not a cross-candidate comparison.
trigger_scope: check-dependencies run on a recognised manifest

applicability.action: report an error when an existing manifest cannot be read or decoded as UTF-8 or BOM-tagged UTF-16, and skip its semantic checks
applicability.exceptions: BOM-tagged UTF-16 is accepted; missing files are handled separately

distinguishing_scenario: A .csproj saved in a legacy code page with invalid UTF-8 bytes: the checker reports an error asking to save it as UTF-8 or BOM-tagged UTF-16, whatever its dependency content.
proposed_clause_text: A manifest that cannot be read or decoded as UTF-8 (or BOM-tagged UTF-16) is reported as an error asking to save it in a readable encoding; its dependency checks are not run.
rationale: check-dependencies.cjs:217-220 verified. The UTF-8 editor default (FG-K0-29c85ea2a9) is a formatting preference with no checker consequence, and the fail-closed pre-command input decoding (FG-K0-2d8a0332f6) concerns hook input; no K0 group states that an undecodable manifest is a check error. Distinct designed acceptance gate.

applicability.action: report an error when a ``` fence in a non-code instruction artifact is never closed
applicability.enforcement: static code read (fences() lines 58-72, used at 199), not executed
applicability.exceptions: only backtick fences are recognised; code artifacts are not fence-parsed

distinguishing_scenario: A knowledge skill ending with an opening ```csharp line and no closing fence: headers and classification valid, the checker reports 'code fence is never closed'.
proposed_clause_text: A backtick code fence that is never closed in an instruction artifact is an instruction-check error.
rationale: check-instructions.cjs:58-72 and 198-199 verified. Both runs mentioned 'malformed fences reported' only in IMPLEMENTATION coverage notes; the K0 instruction-checker groups (classification, header, unclassified files) contain no fence condition. An otherwise valid artifact fails solely because a fence stays open, so this is an unrepresented checker gate.

applicability.action: accept a closing fence only when the trimmed line is exactly three backticks, otherwise report an error and keep the fence open
applicability.trigger: a backtick-prefixed line inside an open fence

distinguishing_scenario: A block opened with ```` and closed with ````: valid Markdown, the checker reports the closing line and then 'never closed'.
proposed_clause_text: Inside an open code fence, a backtick-prefixed line closes the fence only if it is exactly three backticks; any other backtick-prefixed line is reported as an error.
rationale: check-instructions.cjs:62-69 verified: inside an open fence, any line starting with ``` other than exactly ``` reports 'a closing code fence must stand on its own line'. This rejects four-backtick fences and info-string closers that Markdown accepts; distinct from the end-of-file condition in CIS-K0-0005 (a different trigger). No K0 group states it.
